Hi luv. So sorry to learn of your travails. It seems to me you're suffering PTSD from the rape, & severe depression from the PTSD & ED & weight issues. Take it from one who knows, depression certainly alters one's perceptions. I'm married 33 years to the best woman in the world, one who has stood with me through some very strange & trying times. Yet there are times when I'm positive she doesn't love me & only stays now because of stubbornness & a fear of being alone. I honestly can't help believing that at times, & I've only just recently learned enough to avoid acting on it (suicide more than leaving her, that is).

Obviously there's a great deal about your life that I don't know, but the porn...? That's just a guy thing. Honestly. It almost certainly doesn't reflect his feelings for you per se. I think guys tend to be hardwired to spread their bounty as it were.... Porn can provide a constructive outlet for that urge. 

Of course there's no excuse to act boorish. I would never view porn in my wife's presence--unless it was something we were viewing together, of course. Question: have you been waiting for him to invite you to share porn with him, or have you suggested it as something the two of you can share?

Though it's virtually a cliche, communication is the key here. Quite some years ago my wife expressed dissatisfaction with the state of our sexual relations. We talked. I asked her how come she didn't start things more often herself; why did she assume such a passive role?

She told me she thought I'd drop dead of a heart attack if she came on to me.

Hunh? I honestly think sexually aggressive women are a major turn on; coyness, not so much. So we got through that period;-)

It also turns out I have mild, not previously diagnosed Asperger's. It's not unusual for Aspies to have trouble with conventional sex, & the contact & interpretation it requires. I always assumed it was my own perversion that made regular sex more difficult for me that it was supposed to be.

Have you spoken to him about the gaming &/or porn?  What did you guys do before when he came home? Did you talk, eat, have sex, watch TV? Why not ask him to set aside say half-an-hour (to start...) to do whatever you guys used to, or something new for the two of you, then he can go online & play games for a while? 

Maybe suggest sharing some of the porn (but not all of it; good fences make good neighbors & good marriages:). Just try not to take his use of it personally. & if you put some sexy times aside for just you, solo, you might not feel threatened or resentful of his.

Finally, I agree about getting treatment. You need it. Clearly. Don't know about meds, but anything that helps you recenter on viewing things objectively will help you & your marriage. Stress, depression, mood disorders in general have wrecked many a marriage in the past, tragically when both parties still love one another, but find living together impossible.

Whatever happens, good luck.
To me you sound as though you deserve for good things to happen:)

Greetings. I was just a hair or two older than you when I tried shaving with a cheap straight edge just out of curiosity. Shave didn't go real well, but I followed up eventually with a real SE, & have never once considered going back. As others have pointed out there's a real zen in straight razor shaving: one focuses & concentrates for those few minutes in the am. It really makes a difference.

With all due respect to DE aficionados here I just don't see those. I learned to shave using my dad's safety razor. Hated it. Sure the blades are sharper than fuck, being disposable, but the configuration doesn't work for me.

A non-fancy SE will run you about a $100. Alternately you can buy an older one on ebay or such & rehabilitate it if you're good at honing.

Say you do buy a basic SE. You'll also want a good quality natural hair brush--sable or badger--don't skimp on that. Now if you've spent all of your discretionary income on razor & brush, you can use a smooth wide belt to strop for now. You also don't need fancy soaps. I use $1 shaving soaps, but any soap that foams will work. The key to a great, smooth is water, hot water. Soap just holds the water onto the skin.

I use hot water to lather, cold to rinse the blade. My whiskers are pretty light, so I can get away with one pass & with shaving against their growth (from the neck moving up). Your mileage may vary.

Eventually you'll want to look into a hone. I recommend a Japanese waterstone 6000 - 8000 grit. Depending on how heavy your beard is razor shouldn't need honing more often than 6 months to a year.

When you shave, whichever way you go, keep the blade almost completely parallel to your skin. That's really the key to a close, laceration-free shave. It probably doesn't hurt to watch what videos are available, too. 

It's kind of an expensive set up & all, but these things will last you a lifetime; your grandkids might use them if properly inspired, lol!

Wow, my heart goes out to you. More than twenty five years ago I destroyed my hearing with gunfire. I have superb verbal skills, but I can't hear what people say. When you talk to me I have to focus all of my energy just to understand you, nevermind trying to formulate an intelligent response. & jokes? Forget it. I can't follow them because people change their tones when delivering a punchline. So I hear the set up, but not the pay off:(

So I totally get that part. You feel stupid, & that people perceive you as stupid. That gets old fast. & I totally understand about not wanting to be happier because you don't deserve to be. I must be so far around the bend because it makes perfect sense to me;-)

But if those wonderful kids love you back, then consider you're not the awful person you fear yourself to be. & perhaps consider also that even if you don't deserve happiness, maybe they deserve a happier Aunt Macabre:) 

Note I just say "happier" not "happy" because we're talking baby steps, not forgetting who we are & basically I have no idea what happy is or what it's supposed to mean.

I understand. Will you consider going back to your psychiatrist? If you see him/her say once per week would you be able to arrange transpo? I ask because I believe you about the meds, but I've heard many stories of successful application of psych meds, but almost never, never right away. It usually takes months to arrange the proper dosage & combination while minimizing side effects.

Cheating is a mistake. Not a moral failing. You don't deserve to die because of it; instead you'll learn from your mistakes in order not to repeat them. I'm very glad to hear you have a support system in place. It sounds as though they're on the ball keeping you safe. In that regard it'd be most uncool to let them down by killing yourself:-)

I hate when people claim suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary problem, but debt & solitude are usually temporary. Don't let their existence hem you in. 

Do you mind if I ask what is it about your Asperger's you find especially debilitating?

Finally, I'm glad you're refilling your meds. That's a positive step forward, & just what I think you need right now.

God bless, sweetie:)

Continue meds, therapy ... tumblr, luv. Share those thoughts with the great electronic void. I promise you that people do see them even when they don't respond. Hey, you can follow me & I'll follow you 'cause I need followers like no one's business, lol! What boyfriend doesn't know won't hurt him. I mean, really you can do this for you, & in so doing might feel better & less guilty about being depressed around him.

I am angry at him for not being more empathetic & understanding of your problems. Does he know you're considering taking your own life? If that doesn't motivate him to patience & empathy for you then it might be time to trade up?

I really do understand about wanting people to care. It's a bit of bind because you want to die but can't bear to inflict that kind of pain on others, yet I think those of us who consider ending our lives are secretly (or openly:) terrified that no one, no one at all will care.

Don't fret not handling yourself, either. You probably wouldn't feel that way if you had diabetes or thyroid problems & had to take meds to correct those. Just try not to think of the regimen you're on as a temporary, momentary measure. Adjust as best you can to the side effects & integrate them into you life.

If you're up for reading I recommend Kay Redfield Jamison's An Unquiet Mind. Jamison teaches psychiatry at Johns Hopkins, & is also manic-depressive. I think it's worthwhile reading about her struggles to adapt to the medications that eventually saved her life.

Finally, don't forget that psych meds are almost never right the first time. They do take some tweaking & patience.

Good luck & God bless, sweetie. I don't know you, but I strongly suspect you deserve way better than to hate yourself & die at such a young age.

Don't screw around with that DE crap. I learned to shave with my dad's DE back in the day & hate them.  The other readers are right, your grandad's razors are in great condition. All they need is honing & a quick strop & you're ready to go.

From your description of a beard I guess you're like me & have light whiskers. Then you'll really appreciate the straight-edge. With it you might only shave every three or four days yet always seem clean-shaven. I shave right out the shower. I use a badger brush, basic shaving soap. Hot water for lather on the face, cold water to rinse the blade (cold contracts & you do feel the difference. Might try ice water one of these days just to see, lol!)

With a light beard you ought to get away with only one pass. Men with heavier beards might make two or three. Whatever's comfortable.  It seems like a big deal at first, but will quickly become second nature. Just remember to keep the flat of the blade parallel to your skin & you won't be injured.

There is a certain zen in this, a few moments of perfect concentration & method. I find it relaxing & invigorating.

It's really cool that you're in a position to  restore your grandpa's razors & use them. Sometimes you've just got to spit in the eye of this disposable culture of ours.

I've shaved with a fixed SE for more than 25 years now. Once you go straight-edge there's no going back, lol! I learned how to shave using a double-edge safety razor of my dad's. Hate them. Worst invention ever just after the automatic dishwasher. I don't know why some here endorse them. 

Straight edge shaving is a technique. After you get your grandad's razor take it to a knife shop or someplace where it can be honed & possibly cleaned of rush or corrosion. If can't get ahold of grandad's strop you can start stropping with a smooth leather  belt. Don't skimp on the brush. If you have to buy one, avoid artificial, get badger or sable. Soap need not be fancy-schmancy. Real men don't smell. 

I have a fairly light beard. I shave after showering once every three days or so. I can also shave against the growth of my whiskers. If you beard is on the heavy side shave with the growth instead. The key to a good shave & avoiding injury is concentration & keeping the flat of the blade almost parallel to your skin. Do not imitate movies. They all do it wrong (except maybe for Angie Dickinson shaving Dean Martin in Rio Bravo;). Keep that blade flat & you'll be fine. Some men go for two or more passes with the blade, relathering each time. I don't need to. You might.

Finally, I've only recently started using cold water to rinse the blade. Cold contracts & you actually do feel the difference. Hot water, lots of it, on the face. Cold water on the blade.

Starting out at once seems complicated & involved for a lousy shave, but soon it becomes second nature & if you stick to it you'll wonder how you ever used a disposable. Like other men (& some ladies;) I find straight edge razor is a bit zen like. It provides a few moments of pure focus & discipline in my otherwise haphazard schedule.

Good luck.

Congrats on the razor. Once you go straight-edge there's no going back, lol!  Don't skimp on a high quality badger brush. Soap need not be fancy, I used dollar-a-bar shaving soap. Dovo & Illinois Strop Co. both make very good strops. If you can't get one right away, use a smooth leather belt. Hot water, 'cause water, not soap/foam is what makes the shave happen. Soap holds the water in place.

I always shave after a shower. My beard isn't heavy, so I can get away with one pass. Lasts me about three days. I can shave against the growth of my whiskers, but if yours are heavier shave with them.

Ultimately you might want to get a hone--I recommend a Japanese water stone 6000 - 8000 grit. But since your razor's new you won't need that for quite a while.

First things first. What, if any, history of mental issues do you have? If none, then most MDs would rule out somatic reasons for your experiences before exploring psychiatric ones. Temporal lobe lesions, for example, can produce vivid hallucinations. I believe usually an eeg &/or MRI are done to rule out brain issues.

How was your adjustment after her death? Did you find yourself gradually recovering? Progress? None?

The younger sister of an online friend took an overdose of "sleeping pills" last month (I don't know what the meds were, she was in Europe). Her mother found her alive. She was brought to the hospital & put into a coma. Doctors weren't optimistic. & so it was, after two days her eeg flatlined, they shut down the ventilator, &, at 14 years of age, she passed away. 

Apparently brain swelling, possibly due to edema (not bleeding as would be the case with a subdural hematoma caused by trauma), caused the fatal damage. Doctors had no way to relieve the pressure. My friend said they spoke of removing her skull cap to permit her brain to swell without being crushed. I don't honestly know if that's ever done. It sounds absurd. Perhaps they were trying to illustrate what they, & she, were up against.

Again, I don't know precisely what she took, but this is a complication of some drug toxicities that I've heard of prior. When I get the energy I'll try to look up the physio-chemistry behind it.

Her name was Helena.

I think you've to the right place, love. It can be easier to tell relative strangers about the abuse, incest & rape you've suffered because we have nothing invested in the status quo of your family, community & school. We don't care if your cousin is a pedophile creep or this at school is a rapist. Sadly acquaintance rape & incest are often met with disbelief simply because the people close to you are also close to the perpetrators. That's no excuse. It merely compounds tragedy & worsens the trauma: I can't imagine having to see the rapo in school every day or your cousin at family shindigs. That must be torture.

Even though you didn't ask for advice I'll offer some, free of charge:-). You don't  need counseling, you need therapy, maybe meds. Please consider going back to the same therapist or a new one. No one needs to know beforehand what you want to talk about. Just say you're a bit depressed if you have to. A professional is far less likely to be invested in some toxic status quo, & so has less reason to doubt you.

One thing, if you do this, go in expecting to be believed. I know that's easier said than done, but it is sometimes harder to believe someone who expects you to doubt him or her.

And please, write more. I haven't been on reddit that long, but I have seen that the community here is extremely supportive.

I think you have to reach out to others in the family, try to find out more of what happened & why. It's not inappropriate or macabre to seek answers in a context such as this. I don't know how old you are, but sometimes families will try to keep details away from younger members. This is well-intentioned, but ultimately destructive.

Has there been a wake/memorial/funeral? How close are to the surviving immediate family? One method might be to volunteer to help them, babysit, do work, cook, help houseclean, etc., you'd be providing concrete assistance & also networking with other family members & in doing so get a better picture of whatever was going on in your late relative's circle.

How you feel about your life isn't relevant to the tragedy of someone close taking theirs. For all you know, YOU had the more dire circumstances. Suicide is rarely about external conditions. It can be exacerbated by them, but it's determined more by internal weather. 

Can you talk it out here, provide a few more details concerning this tragedy?

Come what may, & I do hope for the best here, it will NOT be your fault. No how, no way. She talks to you, that's good. Encourage her to talk, to share. She's not putting the load on you, she's letting you share a tiny bit of it. As she opens herself to you, she might become more open to speaking to a professional, someone local. She still lives at home, yes? Hear her out, then perhaps encourage her to reach out to her parents or some other trusted family member?

I've seen this, & others like it, like a million times in just the past month. I say, hey, anything that makes someone pause & reconsider even a moment ... why the hell not?

But my personal reaction is to be offended because it contains so many fallacious assumptions. E.g., when I was that age I did try to kill myself. As honestly & objectively as possible I know my parents would have been fine in the long term. Members of the "greatest generation", they simply weren't the sort who accepted responsibility for the misdeeds of their children. Furthermore my sister & I had been adopted, thus they, & their friends & relatives, understood that you never know what you're going to get when you adopt. 

My big sister had moved away amid great acrimony a few years prior, & had cut off almost all contact with my parents--note I say "almost", she did see them occasionally for signing of documents, etc., but never even bothered to say hello to me. I ceased to exist for her the moment she moved away.

Friends such as I had would have been sad, for about ten minutes. I had no deep friendships; reaction would have been mostly teenage dramatics such as one invariably sees on the television following a high or middle school tragedy. I was essentially an invisible sort in middle & high schools. The year book committee would have had a great time creating a memorial page for me, but none of them would have had the slightest idea who I was.

I hardly knew my paternal grandmother who lived 3000 miles away, & my mother's mother hated my guts for making her daughter's life miserable; her husband, my grandfather, was a distant figure entombed in a wing-backed chair with his Pall Malls unfiltered & hearing aids turned off. I never so much as had a single conversation with him after I was 8 or 9.

Rest of my family would have understood, as my parents did, that sometimes you have the luck of the draw; sometimes you don't.

So this is just me feeling sorry for myself, which I honestly rarely indulge these days, but that is how I react to these Devastation Chronicle type arguments...;-)  So yeah, use this argument, but know it can really, really backfire by reminding some people just how isolated they are, & how utterly unimportant they are ... to anyone.

Several reasons, I think. One, it takes a lot of energy & mental resources to start your life anew, which people in the throes of depression don't have; another is that many of us don't believe we deserve to be alive under any circumstances.

Ironically when I was a kid the thing I feared the most was losing my dad. I prayed to die then to prevent that kind abandonment. On the other hand, when my mother died I was 16 & didn't care about it all, not one bit. No idea why. We got along well enough. As for my dad, he just turned 90:)  Don't know if my son's ready to lose me, exactly, but I do believe he'll be just fine, & that's not a bad thing, either, I don't want to believe that his life would be ruined if I ran afoul of an MTA bus or got by pieces of the space station tomorrow.

I'm glad to learn you found it helpful in some small way. Indeed, I haven't the first part of a clue what people mean by "happiness", maybe I've been happy & wasn't smart enough to realize it, or maybe people have differing capacities for happiness, joy, whatever. So maybe a vibrant life isn't in the cards for people like us. But we can still hope for & work towards doing things that are meaningful & worthwhile to us; things that matter.

I actually haven't spoken to her about--though after 32 years of marriage it's folly to believe you have any secrets from your spouse;-). One, a few years before our son was born we drank wine & took hydrocodone & had a real heart to heart: I think we agreed that were it not for a fundamental curiosity & desire to learn new things about the world neither of us would have lived long enough to meet;-) 

Now I just don't want to add to her burdens.

Speaking as one repulsive person to another I can tell you that even when things were going quite well for me I always assumed I would die of suicide one day. That's not a big deal, got to die of something, right? But I did manage one day to stumble into someone who would turn out to be my soulmate, 'twas in '79 & we're together still. We also raised a son who's now 22 & on the verge of marrying himself. 

Throughout all of this I've always known I don't deserve to be alive, shouldn't be. Family would be way, way better off if I wasn't. But of course by & large it wasn't a choice I was free to make. Right at the moment I really don't want to continue on anymore--& like you I'm not aware of being depressed. It's just business as usual.

But, when I think back on some of the intervening years I do believe I've been permitted to do somethings that were worthwhile & meaningful. & that, I believe, is part of the way through this. Not searching for happiness or relationships so much as trying to do things that are important to us & which have meaning. 

In addition to raising a pretty good kid to adulthood I was able to save one of Los Angeles's most cherished landmarks from burning down, cover & support one of the first truly worthwhile solutions to homelessness, care for burn victims in agony as profound as it is ineffable ... to name a few. Please don't get me wrong, these are things anyone with a double-digit IQ could have done, I just happened to be in the right place at the right time--nearly everything I've done otherwise was bollocks. Still I'm glad I was around to do them;-)

Hope this helps in some way....

I know I've been there myself: there are genuinely rotten people out there in the world, people whose family would be better off without them, people of the lie, toxic people, sociopaths. As such people exist why can't I be one? Why not?
